title: Elvin Jones and Blakey: loving yet fierce on stage
summary: Jackson compares Elvin Jones and Blakey as supportive, loving men who never shortchanged an audience, yet were 'The Volcano' and 'Thunder' on stage.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And you’ve had this experience with, fortunately, catching him and Elvin Jones right at the end of their careers. That’s fortunate I guess.

Well yeah, fortunate for me. Also just the way my life worked out, that towards the end of their careers and their lives and so it just signals that there was a kind of changing of the era, with the passing of these musicians. Elvin was a very, very special person, much in the way of Art, very supportive, very loving, of the diaspora in general. Very, I mean in love with jazz music is what I’m saying, just in love with the musicians. I mean obviously when he spoke of John Coltrane there was a reverence, when he spoke of Charlie Parker, when he spoke of Billie Holiday, when he spoke of his friends, in addition to his brothers, but he just had a loving feeling and the utmost responsibility for the music that he was trying to play. And so I think that’s something that Art and Elvin had in common, that they really never shortchanged anyone. No one can ever say they went to see Elvin Jones or Art Blakey and they got shortchanged. It’s impossible. You always got your money’s worth.

That’s true. I remember seeing him in a club once and I thought he was fearsome. I mean you say he was a loving person on stage, but I mean he would sweat and you would see his teeth and you said man, this man is —

Well that was the look of his presentation. And so I’m not saying that he wasn’t very dynamic and very strong, but I mean in a conversation with Elvin, he was so articulate and so specific in his thoughts about the music and his ideas, and his feelings towards the musicians. And so that’s what I mean in terms of a very loving appreciation for him to have been able to have played the drums with these different artists. But obviously on © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

stage he was a killer, to coin a phrase. But I mean he absolutely was. There was nothing about him that was — it was loving but it still had a certain energy and passion that you know, Art was called “The Volcano” by Dizzy and Elvin was nicknamed “Thunder.”
So that probably speaks to what you’re talking about.
